title: Caltrain crew rules, operator competition and track-access costs
question: What cash, competition and permit effects can be established from the published operating rules?
finding: The published records trace a change to seven-car staffing, a proposed two-year shift in operator procurement, and a full-shift charge for shorter third-party work. Measuring the effects requires payroll, bids and invoices.
how: Matched the dates and terms in nine original agency documents, including the rail operator procurement plans, operating statistics, site support rules and committee records.
limits: Conditional extensions, estimated avoided costs, fee estimates and published scheduling rules must be tested against executed agreements and actual transactions.

rows.test: Did the original seven-car crew rule survive electrification?
rows.record: In 2018 Caltrain said a third conductor was required on trains longer than six cars. In 2020 staff described removing the requirement in exchange for a $4.1 million one-time item and a $525,000 annual performance bonus pool. The $8 million–$10 million annual figure was a forecast of avoided cost. FY2025 records confirm seven-car electric sets entered all-day service on September 21, 2024.
rows.limit: Request the signed conductor work rule, the FY2021 disbursement, bonus-pool payments, actual on-duty staffing by train length and the first full-year comparison with the forecast. The cited budget provision and forecast do not establish either net savings or waste.

source.t: Contract extension staff analysis, PDF page 16

comparison.t: 2018 staff answer on crew size and passenger needs, PDF page 4

payment.t: FY2025 report on actual service, PDF page 11

rows.test: Why did staff move the planned transition to the next rail operator back two years?
rows.record: May 2025 planning set July 1, 2027 as the transition date. In October staff proposed negotiating a two-year extension, pointing to an overlapping Boston-area operator procurement, uncertain funding, and time for a handover. The April 2026 finance packet still described negotiations toward June 30, 2029. The forecast and negotiation explain timing; they do not establish that the extension was signed or that an interested bidder was excluded.
rows.limit: Request the federal concurrence, signed extension and award resolution, the final solicitation calendar and market outreach or bidder withdrawal records.

source.t: May 2025 original procurement timetable, PDF page 25

payment.t: 2026 finance packet, proposed extension still in negotiation, PDF page 72

rows.test: What costs can fall on an applicant requesting only part of a day of railroad support?
rows.record: Caltrain’s third-party project guidance says operator personnel are paid for a full eight- or ten-hour day even on shorter jobs. Its published estimate for a flagger is about $1,500 per day. The railroad’s work-planning policy asks for five days of notice for cancelling scheduled work supported by its personnel or equipment unless the individual contract specifies another period.
rows.limit: A published rate and a shift minimum do not show a particular project was overcharged or delayed. Request permits, planned and actual shifts, cancellations, vendor invoices and actual reimbursements for a defined project sample.

source.t: Caltrain third-party support and full-day rule

comparison.t: Caltrain posted estimates for flaggers and other support

payment.t: Safe work planning, cancellation notice, PDF page 11
